title: Transitivity of colimits over directed pair systems
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, with colimits understood as in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $I$ and $K_i$ for $i\in I$ be small nonempty directed preordered sets. Suppose $P=\{(i,k):i\in I,\ k\in K_i\}$ has a preorder $\preceq$ such that (a) $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$ implies $i\le j$; (b) $k\le l$ in $K_i$ implies $(i,k)\preceq(i,l)$; and (c) for every $i\le j$ and $k\in K_i$ some $l\in K_j$ satisfies $(i,k)\preceq(j,l)$. Let $D:P\to\mathcal C$ and $B:I\to\mathcal C$ be functors. Suppose maps $b_{ik}:D(i,k)\to B_i$ satisfy $B(i\le j)b_{ik}=b_{jl}D((i,k)\preceq(j,l))$ for every relation in $P$, and that for each $i$ the maps $(b_{ik})_{k\in K_i}$ exhibit $B_i$ as the colimit of $D$ restricted along $K_i\to P$, $k\mapsto(i,k)$. If $(L,(c_i)_i)$ is a colimit cocone of $B$, then $(L,(c_i b_{ik})_{(i,k)\in P})$ is a colimit cocone of $D$. Thus the canonical comparison $\varinjlim_PD\to\varinjlim_IB$ is an isomorphism whenever the right-hand colimit exists.

proof.text: Write $d_{qp}=D(p\preceq q)$ and $B_{ji}=B(i\le j)$, with composition read right to left. The dependent union $P$ is small. Condition (a) makes the projection $P\to I$ monotone, and (b) makes each inclusion $K_i\to P$ monotone, hence a functor of the associated thin categories. For $p=(i,k)\preceq q=(j,l)$, compatibility gives $(c_jb_{jl})d_{qp}=c_jB_{ji}b_{ik}=c_ib_{ik}$. Thus the proposed legs form a cocone on $D$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

proof.text: Let $(M,(a_{ik}))$ be an arbitrary cocone on $D$. Its restriction along $K_i\to P$ is a cocone, since condition (b) supplies each required pair relation. The assumed fiber colimit and [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] give a unique $u_i:B_i\to M$ with $u_ib_{ik}=a_{ik}$ for all $k\in K_i$.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, final displayed colimit equality; explicit universal-property argument using Categories, Tag 002F, definition-colimit.

proof.text: Fix $i\le j$. For each $k\in K_i$, condition (c) supplies $l\in K_j$ with $p=(i,k)\preceq q=(j,l)$. The given compatibility and the cocone equation for $a$ imply $u_jB_{ji}b_{ik}=u_jb_{jl}d_{qp}=a_{jl}d_{qp}=a_{ik}=u_ib_{ik}$. Both $u_jB_{ji}$ and $u_i$ therefore factor the same cocone on the $i$th fiber; uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $u_jB_{ji}=u_i$. This proves compatibility without choosing transition functors between the fibers.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, final displayed colimit equality; explicit universal-property argument using Categories, Tag 002F, definition-colimit.

proof.text: The compatible family $(u_i)$ is a cocone on $B$ with vertex $M$. Since $(L,(c_i))$ is a colimit of $B$, [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives a unique $u:L\to M$ with $uc_i=u_i$. Consequently $u(c_ib_{ik})=u_ib_{ik}=a_{ik}$, so $u$ factors the arbitrary cocone on $D$.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, final displayed colimit equality; explicit universal-property argument using Categories, Tag 002F, definition-colimit.

proof.text: Suppose $v:L\to M$ also satisfies $v(c_ib_{ik})=a_{ik}$ for every pair. For fixed $i$, the maps $vc_i$ and $u_i$ agree after every $b_{ik}$, so fiber-colimit uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $vc_i=u_i$. Base-colimit uniqueness then gives $v=u$. Thus the cocone of step 1 has the full existence and uniqueness property of a colimit of $D$.

source.place: Tag 0817, lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite, final displayed colimit equality; explicit universal-property argument using Categories, Tag 002F, definition-colimit.

proof.text: Existence of the base colimit therefore provides a colimit of $D$. Put $s_{(i,k)}=c_ib_{ik}$. If $(C,(t_p))$ is a chosen colimit of $D$, its universal property gives $f:C\to L$ with $ft_p=s_p$. The colimit property just proved for $L$ gives $g:L\to C$ with $gs_p=t_p$. Then $(gf)t_p=gs_p=t_p$ and $(fg)s_p=ft_p=s_p$ for every $p$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives $gf=1_C$ and $fg=1_L$. The canonical comparison $f$ is thus an isomorphism.
